dim_builds.name: complete_status_ids
dim_builds.output: small flat array / bitmask of int32 (size 4)

dim_builds.name: chn_set
dim_builds.predicate: name IS NOT NULL AND (memmem(name,'man') OR memmem(name,'Man'))
dim_builds.notes: ~3% selectivity; bitset uses ~393KB, faster lookup than hash_set

join_order.notes: title is driver; mk filter (kw_set IN 10 of 134170) is ~0.0075% per mk row, but per-title ~0.05% titles survive

join_order.strategy: index_range_probe + subject==cast_id AND status_id IN complete_status_ids
join_order.notes: complete_cast 135k rows; only titles with matching cc survive
also captures candidate mi_idx.info string_views for MIN

join_order.strategy: index_range_probe + chn_set membership; fetch n.name via person_id-1
join_order.notes: cast_info is largest fact (36M); only probe within ranges of surviving t_ids

filters.predicate: subject_id == cast_id AND status_id IN complete_status_ids

data_structures.complete_status_ids: small int32 array (sorted, linear search OK; size 2)
data_structures.aggregation: 4 string_view MIN trackers (chn.name, mi_idx.info, n.name, t.title) with copy-on-update into local buffer

parallelism.reduction: per-thread MIN trackers reduced at end (4 string_views)

notes: Driver: title scan. For each title row, apply year+kind filters cheaply (int32). Then sequentially probe the four fact ranges via offsets indexes in order of selectivity (mk most selective). Within each surviving title, iterate ci range, test chn_set membership and project n.name (person_id-1). Capture candidate (chn.name, mi_idx.info, n.name, t.title) tuples and update 4 separate per-thread MIN trackers. Pre-build chn_set as bitset since char_name is dense PK. Pre-build kw_set as hash_set since only 10 entries.
